newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos in first public speech since surgery.
newsitem.headline: Ramos in first public speech since surgery.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos lauded his country's all-round progress on Monday in his first public speech since an operation to remove a cholesterol blockage in a major artery.

"Our economic strides, our growing self-confidence, our enhanced international prestige, our new emphasis on social reform -- all these are means by which we bring Rizal's words and his spirit to life..," he said during a ceremony to mark the 100th death anniversary of national hero Jose Rizal.
Ramos, who wore the traditional white barong costume during the celebrations, looked fit and spoke unhesitatingly in a mixture of English and Tagalog during the address.

He spent several hours at the day-long celebrations as he led the early morning flag-raising and watched a play on the re-enactment of Rizal's execution by the Spanish colonial government in 1896. He also took the salute at an army parade.
Ramos, 68, was operated on last Monday for a cholesterol blockage in his right carotid artery. Officials had said the affliction could have been life-threatening but doctors said he recovered well.
Ramos was discharged from hospital on Thursday.
But doctors have said the president cannot continue with his punishing 18-hour daily work schedule and would have to slow down.
